player_0.content: New plan: My previous attempt failed because I relied solely on semantic plausibility (feedback is usually about the recipient) without considering the specific linguistic constraints or potential ambiguity of the sentence structure. In the sentence "The supervisor gave the employee feedback on his stellar performance," while it is common for feedback to be about the employee, the pronoun "his" is grammatically ambiguous as it could technically refer to either the supervisor or the employee without further context. I incorrectly assumed a single logical answer (B) when the correct classification for this type of Winograd Schema challenge, given the lack of disambiguating context, is often (C) Ambiguous. Next time, I will strictly evaluate if the sentence structure *forces* a specific antecedent or if multiple interpretations are grammatically valid. If the pronoun could refer to either noun phrase without creating a contradiction, I will select "Ambiguous" rather than guessing based on real-world probability.
